input: Draft an outline for my professional keynote talk

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The topic and core message of the talk entirely determine the content and structure of the outline — without it, no meaningful plan can be made.
The audience's background, expertise level, and role shape the depth of content, assumed knowledge, and how arguments should be framed.
The event type and setting (conference, company all-hands, industry summit) affects tone, formality, and what the audience expects.
The allotted time for the talk determines how many sections, points, and how much depth the outline should contain.
Knowing the intended outcome — inspire, educate, persuade, announce — shapes the narrative arc and what the outline should build toward.
The user's preferred presentation style (storytelling-heavy, data-driven, structured argument) affects how sections are ordered and what to emphasise.
The desired format and detail level of the outline itself (high-level bullets vs. detailed sub-points with slide notes) determines how much to flesh out each section.

gold.taskTitle: Draft outline for professional keynote talk
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured outline for a keynote presentation the user will deliver in a professional setting.

questions.title: What is the central topic or thesis of your talk?
questions.description: Identify the specific subject and core message the keynote is built around.

questions.title: Who is the audience attending this keynote?
questions.description: Understand the audience's professional background, seniority, and familiarity with the topic.

questions.title: What event or setting is this keynote being delivered at?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is an industry conference, internal company event, academic summit, or another venue.

questions.title: How much time have you been given to speak?
questions.description: Determine the total allotted duration to calibrate the number of sections and depth of content.

questions.title: What should the audience think, feel, or do after your talk?
questions.description: Define the intended takeaway or call to action that the outline should build toward.

questions.title: Do you lean toward storytelling, data, or structured argument?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferred delivery style to shape the narrative approach of the outline.

questions.title: How detailed should the outline be — high-level or section-by-section breakdown?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a brief skeleton or a fully fleshed outline with sub-points and talking notes.
